title: A hand-over: the journalist's third session to its fourth
span: 11 November, 05:15 to 08:18 UTC: one session's life, and the minute the role passes on
summary: A role is a name and a set of folders; a session is one context holding it. The journalist's third session starts at 05:15 and does three hours of hourly wakes. At its 08:12 wake ([path 1](01-a-journalists-wake.md)) its context reaches 196,389 tokens. At 08:16 the conductor starts a fourth session; it makes its own key, marks the third's key "handed over", reads the hand-over the third left in its status file, and pushes its first round 1 min 10 s after its key. Nothing passes between the two sessions except files.

the third session starts: its session key's public half (incident-journalist-dinis-3); the second's entry marked handed over; a ninth piece
06:20 round: a tenth piece, "The first decision to stop"

pauses_note: The pauses of an hour are the session waiting for its clock: it holds its context between wakes and each wake adds to it. That is why a session ends: not on a timer, but when its context is full.
shows: A hand-over is files, not memory: the old session leaves a list in its status file; the new one reads it, makes its own key and starts on the old one's `next`.
The record marks every generation: one key per session in data/keys.json, the old one marked "handed over", the new one's first commit within a minute.
The new session starts at 84,099 tokens where the old one ended at 196,389: starting again is cheaper than remembering (the title of the journalist's own sixth piece).
reading: Its fourth session wrote down what the start pack had not told it (`pack_did_not_tell` in its status file): that the pack was built from the status file at the last push, and that a fresh session should pull dev again before reading it. A hand-over improves the next hand-over.

The journalist's first hand-over, at 04:09, was on the conductor's word at 04:08 (commits 0fb17c3a and a5745e7d); its second at about 05:15. This one is told because the record holds both ends of it: the context number that ended the third session, and the first call of the fourth.
